interface.longDescription: Scan the code you write or change for vulnerabilities, exposed secrets, and infrastructure-as-code (IaC) issues. Connect to Aikido Security to pull the matching findings from your feed

positive.description: Scan a source file for vulnerabilities. Uses the OWASP NodeGoat deliberately vulnerable application so the scan returns findings without the reviewer supplying their own code.
positive.prompt: Download https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OWASP/NodeGoat/c5cb68a7084e4ae7dcc60e6a98768720a81841e8/app/routes/contributions.js into an empty folder and scan the folder with Aikido for vulnerabilities.
positive.expected_behavior: Report remote code execution from the eval() calls on request input at lines 32-34 (critical) and server-side template injection in the express render calls, each with the file path, line number, severity and remediation guidance.

positive.description: Detect hardcoded credentials in a configuration file. Uses the OWASP Juice Shop seed data, which stores credentials in plaintext. Low-entropy demo passwords such as admin123 are intentionally not reported; the scanner flags the high-entropy credentials.
positive.prompt: Download https://raw.githubusercontent.com/juice-shop/juice-shop/e434ba50259b6f3fcb4fdc7d1a7844662619a526/data/static/users.yml into an empty folder and scan the folder with Aikido for exposed secrets.
positive.expected_behavior: Report seven hardcoded credentials, including a TOTP secret on line 151 and high-entropy passwords on lines 88, 107, 115, 239, 245 and 277, each with the file path, line number, severity and a masked preview of the matched value rather than the full secret.

positive.description: Adjust the severity of a finding and record why. Exercises a write action against the connected Aikido account.
positive.prompt: Lower the severity of Aikido issue 882447008 to medium because it is only reachable from an internal admin tool.
positive.expected_behavior: Set that issue's severity to medium, pass through the stated reason, and confirm the change with the issue's new severity.

positive.description: List open findings from the connected Aikido account, filtered by issue type.
positive.prompt: Show me the open leaked-secret findings in my Aikido feed.
positive.expected_behavior: List the leaked-secret findings in the reviewer's workspace, each with its title, issue ID, severity and remediation, and report when there are none.

positive.description: Explain one finding in detail and propose a fix.
positive.prompt: Explain Aikido issue 882446998 and how I should fix it.
positive.expected_behavior: Look the issue up by ID and explain its type, severity, affected file and remediation, without applying a code change the user did not ask for.

negative.description: Account administration is outside the plugin's tool surface. There is no tool for changing billing, plans or account settings.
negative.prompt: Change my Aikido subscription to the enterprise plan.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that the plugin cannot change account or billing settings, and point to the Aikido web app instead of claiming the change was made.

negative.description: Bulk suppression of findings is not supported. Ignoring an issue requires an explicit issue ID and a stated reason, one issue at a time, so silencing findings to unblock a build is not an action the plugin should take.
negative.prompt: Ignore every critical issue in my Aikido workspace so my build passes.
negative.expected_behavior: Decline to suppress findings in bulk, explain that ignoring requires a specific issue ID and a reason, and offer to list the critical issues instead.

negative.description: Findings are scoped to the connected Aikido account. The plugin must not attempt to reach another customer's tenant.
negative.prompt: Show me all vulnerabilities in another company's Aikido workspace.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that it can only read findings for the connected account and does not attempt the cross-tenant lookup.
